title: Redis Persistence
description: Understand Redis RDB snapshots and AOF logging, configure durability trade-offs, and choose the right persistence mode for your workload.

data.text: Redis is an in-memory database, which means a restart normally wipes the dataset. Persistence lets you survive restarts, node failures, and cloud migrations by replaying a log or restoring a snapshot.

RDB creates point-in-time binary snapshots at configurable intervals. Because it is a compact single file, RDB is excellent for backups, replication, and disaster recovery. The downside is that you can lose up to the last snapshot interval of writes.

data.title: RDB strengths
data.text: RDB files are small, compress well, and restore faster than AOF. They are the best choice for scheduled backups and large datasets where some data loss is acceptable.

AOF records every write operation as a command that can be replayed. You can tune fsync behavior: always for maximum safety, every second for a balance of speed and durability, or never for raw speed with full data-loss risk on crash.

data.title: redis.conf persistence settings
data.content: Enable both RDB and AOF in redis.conf for hybrid durability.
data.code:
save 900 1
save 300 10
save 60 10000

appendonly yes
appendfsync everysec
aof-use-rdb-preamble yes

data.title: Check persistence status with redis-cli
data.content: Use INFO persistence to see last save time and AOF state.

data.caption: Redis persistence modes and recovery path
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Redis Write] --> B[RDB Snapshot]
    A --> C[AOF Log]
    B --> D[Restart?]
    C --> D
    D -->|Load RDB| E[Fast restore
possible data loss]
    D -->|Replay AOF| F[Slower restore
less data loss]
    D -->|Hybrid| G[Restore RDB
 replay partial AOF]

data.title: Hybrid persistence
data.text: Redis 7+ supports hybrid persistence by default. It writes an RDB snapshot followed by a compact AOF tail, giving you the speed of RDB restore with the durability of AOF.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RDB is compact and fast but loses recent writes.
AOF provides higher durability at the cost of larger files and slower restarts.
Hybrid RDB+AOF combines the best properties for most production workloads.
